agentCan: Build the authorize URL, state verification, code exchange, and refresh loop
Check /account/verify to route users into the right flow

approval.cost: No approval fee is stated. However, a paid API plan is intertwined: 'You can complete the app approval process prior to signing up for a paid plan, but you will not be able to make production calls until a paid plan is activated.' No plan prices are given in the developer docs read
approval.trigger: Approval is required for OAuth apps before production use by other users. 'Dropbox Sign requires production approval for apps using OAuth. That means your app can't be authorized or added by other users until it is approved for production.' The App Approval Overview adds: 'Any customers implementing an OAuth workflow that authorizes users with Dropbox Sign OAuth must submit their app for approval through the Support Assisted Approval process before it can be used in production.' (Embedded Signing/Requesting/Templates apps also require approval; non-embedded, API-key-only workflows do NOT: 'Customers implementing a non-embedded workflow do not need to complete the app approval process.') Pre-approval, you may authorize the app from your OWN account only, for testing/building; the Account Creation Flow is entirely blocked pre-approval ('Your app must be approved for production before this flow is possible'). How to submit: the OAuth Workflow approval form (separate forms exist for Embedded vs OAuth; if your app uses both, only the OAuth form). Required: Website URL; Client ID(s); the billing and access scopes enabled; a link to a screen-recorded demo of the integration; relevant identifiers from the demo (signature_request_id and/or template_id); a list of endpoints used in the demo; and 'a description of how you are using all enabled scopes not shown in the demo recording'. Demo guidance: show a user completing the OAuth flow and authorizing your app, and demonstrate each enabled scope; 'A great demo video will typically be 3-5 minutes long, includes a clear voiceover' (this describes the video, not a review SLA). Review criteria (verbatim): 'The implemented Dropbox Sign workflow is complete (mockups will not be approved)' and 'The API was implemented correctly, ensuring there will be no issues when moving into production'. Process: 'A dedicated API support expert will evaluate the app against the criteria... If we need more informations or a live demo, we'll contact you directly. We won't reject any apps without direct contact.' Shortcut for sibling apps: 'once you have had an app approved via the app approval process, if you have any other apps that share the same code base', email apisupport@hellosign.com 'and we will approve your app without needing to go through the app approval process again'. No public marketplace/listing process is described.
approval.wait: Not stated (no figure in any approval page read)

blockers.detail: 'Once your users have authorized access to your app, any changes to the scopes of the app will remove their authorization and they'll need to complete another OAuth flow to issue a new access token that reflects those scopes.' Choose scopes (and the billing model that gates them) carefully up front.
blockers.howToClear: Finalize the billing model and scope set before the first user authorizes.
blockers.title: Scope changes are a one-way door for existing users

blockers.detail: Scopes are selected in the app settings and applied to all tokens the app issues; they are not passed as a parameter in the authorization URL. Every user completes the flow and grants the app those scopes; you cannot request narrower scopes per user or per connection.
blockers.howToClear: Design the product around one app-level scope set, or maintain separate apps for different access levels.
blockers.title: Scopes live in app settings, not in the authorize request

blockers.detail: Approval without a paid plan still blocks production calls: 'you will not be able to make production calls until a paid plan is activated'. After approval you must also remove test_mode from API requests to send production calls.
blockers.howToClear: Activate the paid plan as part of the launch checklist, alongside approval.
blockers.title: Approval precedes scale, plan precedes calls

alternatives: API key (HTTP Basic auth, key as username): documented for endpoints acting on YOUR OWN account; it is not a way to act on behalf of other users, and non-embedded API-key-only workflows skip app approval entirely

Account Creation Flow (a hybrid of authorization code + resource-owner style): your app creates a Dropbox Sign account for a user who doesn't have one via /account/create with your client_id/client_secret and receives tokens, but the token 'will not work until the user has confirmed their account and authorized your app', and this flow requires production approval
flavor.recommended: An API App using the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow (Dropbox Sign's '3 legged OAuth flow'), with scopes set in the app's settings
flavor.why: The object is an API App, created in the API settings (app.hellosign.com), with a Client ID and Client Secret; OAuth-related settings include the OAuth Callback URL, the event callback URL, and the scopes. A structural difference from most providers: scopes are selected in the app settings and applied to all tokens the app issues; they are NOT passed as a parameter in the authorization URL. The billing model is part of the flavor choice (chosen in app settings): 'Charge users' (full access apps that charge the user you're sending calls on behalf of) vs 'Charge me' (limited access apps that charge you, the app owner). Available scopes differ by model: Charge users gives account_access, signature_request_access, template_access, team_access, api_app_access; Charge me gives basic_account_info and request_signature (send signature requests only).

humanMust: Create the API App in the API settings (app name, OAuth callback URL, event callback URL, scopes), or via the Create API App endpoint using your API key
Choose the billing model ('Charge users' / 'Charge me'), which determines the selectable scopes
Submit the app for production approval via the OAuth Workflow approval form, including the screen-recorded demo
Activate a paid API plan before making production calls
name: Dropbox Sign
nuances: Limited visibility by design: 'your app's visibility into customer activity is limited to signature requests created using your API app. You can't see any signature requests that the user sends directly from their own account.' Under signature_request_access, 'Signature requests must be made with oAuth token in order to access' them.

For new API apps, client_id and client_secret are REQUIRED when refreshing a token; for existing apps they are optional, but Dropbox Sign recommends making them required in app settings. Refresh responses return a fresh refresh_token value.

Deny handling: a user who clicks Deny returns to your callback with only state and no code; your callback must handle the missing-code case. Account-creation flow tokens are inert until activation: tokens issued for a brand-new user don't work until the user clicks the email confirmation and authorizes the app.
The email address on the account that owns the approved app is the sender identity shown on signature requests and the final audit trail; Dropbox Sign recommends making it a generic address.
prerequisites: A Dropbox Sign account for the API settings
The billing model and scope set decided before users authorize
A screen-recorded demo of the full workflow for the approval form

steps.detail: In the API settings: app name (public-facing), OAuth Callback URL, event callback URL, and scopes (split by billing model). Choose the billing model: 'Charge users' (full access) or 'Charge me' (limited). The app has a Client ID and Client Secret.
steps.title: Create and configure the API App

steps.detail: Optionally check whether the user has a Dropbox Sign account via /account/verify to pick the right flow. Send the user to app.hellosign.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<client id>&state=<random>&redirect_uri=<your callback> (redirect_uri, if provided, 'must match the OAuth Callback URL specified in the API app settings'). The user logs in (or signs up), sees your app name and scopes, and clicks Accept or Deny. On Accept you receive code + state (verify state matches); on Deny only state.
steps.title: Send the user to the authorization URL

steps.detail: POST to the OAuth token endpoint (/oauth/token) with state, code, grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, client_secret. Response: access_token, token_type Bearer, expires_in 3600, refresh_token, account_id. Call the API on the user's behalf with Authorization: Bearer (e.g. POST /v3/signature_request/send).
steps.title: Exchange the code; call the API

steps.detail: POST to /oauth/token?refresh with grant_type=refresh_token and the stored refresh_token; store the returned tokens. Refresh works 'as long as they have not revoked authorization to your app and the access scopes have not been changed'.
steps.title: Refresh (about-hourly)

steps.detail: Fill out the OAuth Workflow approval form: Website URL, Client ID(s), billing and access scopes enabled, a link to a screen-recorded demo (show a user completing the OAuth flow and each enabled scope), signature_request_id and/or template_id from the demo, the endpoints used, and a description of any enabled scopes not shown. A dedicated API support expert evaluates the app; 'We won't reject any apps without direct contact.'
steps.title: Submit for production approval

steps.detail: Activate a paid API plan (production calls are blocked without one) and remove test_mode from API requests to send production calls.
steps.title: After approval: activate a paid plan; remove test_mode

tagline: A genuine OAuth 2.0 program behind a human gate: scopes are fixed in the app settings (bound to a 'charge users' or 'charge me' billing model), changing them revokes every user's authorization, and no other user can authorize your app until Dropbox Sign's support-assisted approval, with a recorded demo, says yes.

time.active: ~15 min of app setup + ~1-2 hrs of flow code + demo recording time
time.total: Unknown: approval duration is not stated, and a paid plan must also be active for production calls
